Oaths seeking approval; divine and messenger approval contrasted.
Warning of punishment for opposition to God and messenger.
Hidden intentions exposed; one broad thematic comparison staged, not direct textual correspondence.

candidates.difference: Luke's saying concerns concealed matters becoming known in a different discourse; Qur'an 9:64 concerns apprehension of revelation exposing hypocrites' inner attitudes.

history_dossier.title: Concealment, revelation and public exposure in late antique religious discourse

sections.heading: Qur'anic context
sections.text: Q9:61–65 addresses accusations against the Messenger, oaths of approval, threats of punishment and fear of disclosure; interpret in the wider passage, not as isolated aphorisms.

sections.heading: Comparative lead
sections.text: Luke 12:2 may offer a general hidden-to-revealed motif, but no distinct narrative scene or shared uncommon wording is established.

sections.heading: Chronology and witnesses
sections.text: The Gospel of Luke predates Islam in standard scholarly dating; exact literary history, manuscript variants, original Greek text and version-specific translations have not been collated here. A prior composition date alone cannot demonstrate Qur'anic literary dependence.

sections.heading: Outstanding verification
sections.text: Check Luke 12:1–3 in a critical Greek edition and multiple translations; examine relevant earlier Jewish and Syriac material; evaluate whether this motif is too widespread to justify a verse-level Sources card.
